details.label: Summary
details.text: Storms will increase in coverage and intensity over the new few hours along the cold front from northeast Ohio into parts of western/central New York. Trends will continue to be monitored for watch potential

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Height falls with the upper trough are now spreading across MI and approaching the Lower Great Lakes. Gradual destabilization is underway ahead of the cold front, which extends roughly from western NY into OH. Deepening CU and convective showers are also evident over north-central OH and into northwest PA, and farther northeast along the lake breezes into NY. Given continued heating, lift along the front and at least some cooling aloft, storm coverage and intensity should increase along the effective front over the next several hours. The 18Z PIT sounding shows 40 kt midlevel winds along with stronger speeds in the upper levels, although speeds below 700 mb are generally weak. However, overall wind profiles may increase later today, supporting at least some threat of storm organization. Effective deep-layer shear around 40-45 kt may support cellular storm mode at times, along with smaller-scale bowing structures/line segments as well. Marginal hail and locally strong to damaging gusts may occur through early evening
